subject: Clarify: cloud-zone tenancy, snapshot retention & deletion assurances
messages:
From: Peter Hayes <peter.hayes@medlytics.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: legal@medlytics.com
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redlines - snapshots/backups and 'onshore' deletion language

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our legal team circulated an updated DPA redline (attached) and flagged three questions we need clarified before we can sign:

1) Snapshot/backups: we require that logical or physical backups that contain customer data be deleted within 30 days of termination or at the customer's request. The redline also asks that any backup copies used for disaster recovery be stored only in the agreed jurisdiction(s).

2) Residual copies & immutable snapshots: we see language that allows for longer-term immutable snapshots for DR — we need to understand whether those are stored inside EU-only cloud zones when the account is EU-located.

3) Deletion assurance: we have a clause requesting a certified erasure statement (signed) within 30 days and details on chain-of-custody for key material if BYOK is used.

Can you confirm Redwood's practical playbook for these items and whether you're able to accept the 30-day deletion requirement, or if you have a counterproposal?

Attachment: Medlytics_DPA_Redline_v2.docx (docx)

Best,
Peter
Peter Hayes
Head of InfoSec, Medlytics
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: Peter Hayes <peter.hayes@medlytics.com>
Cc: legal@medlytics.com
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines - snapshots/backups and 'onshore' deletion language

Peter — thanks for the clear summary and for the redline. I pulled together the operational details below and attached our standard erasure playbook so your legal/ops folks can see the steps.

Short answer: we can meet strict residency controls and provide a certified erasure statement, but 30 days for all backup/snapshot scenarios is operationally constraining in some DR configurations. We have two practical options:

- Option A (safer for you): EU-dedicated tenancy + accelerated purge add-on. All primary data, snapshots, and KV caches for the account are kept in the EU cloud zone. We will run a prioritized purge that removes customer-accessible data within 30 days and provide a certified erasure statement. Immutable disaster recovery snapshots (if enabled) would be treated as a carveout but can be placed in an EU-only storage class and rotated to limit retention. This option requires explicit configuration on provisioning and carries a small upcharge.

- Option B (default economics): EU-hosted primary data, 90-day snapshot retention for long-term DR snapshots (encrypted, geo-restricted to EU), routine backups trimmed to 30 days for active datasets. We can provide a deletion certificate within 45 days for the full footprint (including job scheduling and backup rotation windows).

Operational notes:
- Backups vs. immutable snapshots: backups are generally incremental and can be pruned quickly; immutable snapshots are copy-on-write for DR and can be subject to longer retention/immutable window.
- BYOK: if you opt for customer-managed keys, we can perform key destruction/zeroization steps and log the process; we will need access to KMS audit proofs to produce a chain-of-custody summary.
- Evidence: we attach our erasure playbook and a sample certificate. We can also include a short runbook entry for your auditors.

Next steps:
1) Which option would Medlytics prefer (A or B)?
2) If Option A, we'll send a scope addendum with the provisioning checklist and pricing.
3) If Option B, we'll propose the 45-day certificate timeline and a short DPA clause tweak to clarify the DR snapshot carveout.

Attachment: redwood-erasure-playbook.pdf (pdf)

Happy to set a 30-minute call with ops/legal to walk through the playbook.

— Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redlines - snapshots/backups and 'onshore' deletion language

Jasmine / Irene — thanks for the context. My read: Medlytics is reasonable on principle, but a hard 30-day deletion window across every persistence layer (including immutable DR snapshots) is operationally risky for us and for them. Proposed legal posture and practical compromise below.

Legal posture (recommended counter-offer):
- Preserve the customer's right to request deletion of primary data and backups; commit to deleting primary datasets and routine incremental backups within 30 days of a valid request or termination where those copies are not required by law.
- For immutable DR snapshots and long-term disaster recovery copies, propose a carveout: those may have a separate maximum retention of 180 days but must be stored within the contracted EU cloud zone, encrypted with keys where the customer can require BYOK, and documented in the SLA.
- Delivery of a certified erasure statement: commit to providing an erasure certificate within 45 days for the full listed scope (primary + routine backups). For DR immutable snapshots we will include confirmation of rotation/purge windows in the certificate and confirm any outstanding immutable objects and expected purge date.

Wording suggestion (plain):
"Upon termination or upon Customer's verified written request, Redwood will: (a) delete Customer Data from production stores and associated routine backups within thirty (30) days, except to the extent that Redwood is required to retain such data by applicable law or for ongoing litigation hold; (b) for Disaster Recovery immutable snapshots, Redwood will ensure storage within the contractual geographic boundary and will either (i) rotate or purge such snapshots within one hundred eighty (180) days, or (ii) destroy the Customer's encryption key if the Customer elects BYOK, subject to applicable retention requirements; (c) Redwood will provide a written erasure certificate describing the actions taken within forty-five (45) days of completion of the deletion processes described herein."

Operational asks for the account team:
- Confirm whether the customer has DR immutable snapshots enabled today and which cloud zone they selected at onboarding.
- If they want an actual 30-day certified purge for every persistence layer, we should price that as a separate compliance add-on and require provisioning in the EU-dedicated zone.

I'll prepare a short DPA amendment with the above language; Jasmine, if you can confirm preference (Option A or B) we can slot the amendment and pricing.

— Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
